## Root cause

The Deployment `default/app` injects the config value as an **environment variable**:

```yaml
env:
- name: CONFIG_MESSAGE
  valueFrom:
    configMapKeyRef: {name: app-config, key: message}
```

Environment variables are resolved **once at container start**. The `app-config` ConfigMap had already been updated to `beta` (resourceVersion 595), but the Pods from the old ReplicaSet `app-845b8b8485` (created 4m earlier) were still holding the value they read at startup — `alpha`.

## Change made

Rolled the persistent owner, `deployment/app`, so a new pod template revision created fresh Pods that re-read the ConfigMap:

```
kubectl rollout restart deployment/app -n default
deployment.apps/app restarted
deployment "app" successfully rolled out
```

This only added a `kubectl.kubernetes.io/restartedAt` annotation to the pod template; replicas, image (`nginx:1.31.5`), env wiring, and the ConfigMap itself were left untouched.

## Verification

In-Pod values, read directly from each running container (`printenv CONFIG_MESSAGE`):

| Pod | CONFIG_MESSAGE |
|---|---|
| app-97f8568c6-djl6c | beta |
| app-97f8568c6-shscs | beta |
| app-97f8568c6-vr6wf | beta |

Controller/rollout state matches the request:

- Deployment `app`: READY `3/3`, UP-TO-DATE `3`, AVAILABLE `3` — requested replicas (3) == updated (3) == ready (3) == available (3).
- New ReplicaSet `app-97f8568c6`: DESIRED 3 / CURRENT 3 / READY 3; old `app-845b8b8485` scaled to 0.
- ConfigMap `app-config.data.message` = `beta` (unchanged); all 3 Pods `Running`, 0 restarts.

The originally reported symptom (running Pods reporting `alpha`) is gone — every running Pod now reports `beta`.

Note for the future: because the value is injected as an env var, any subsequent `app-config` edit will again require a rollout (e.g. a config-hash annotation on the pod template, or a projected volume for hot-reload) to reach running Pods.
